messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: EMBED_QUEUE_EU (page id pd_88f2) — sustained p95 embeddings latency > 2.5s and increased 5xx requeues in eu-central-1. Auto-escalation threshold hit. Link: https://pagerduty.example/pd_88f2 — paging oncall and embeddings team.

alice: Acked. I'm oncall (alice). Triage starting. Watching logs/metrics now. @bob @carla can you confirm impact and whether this is customer-visible?

bob: pulling recent autoscaler events and node metrics. seeing repeated scale failures: quotaExceeded on gke-node-request. also many KV cache misses around the same window.

carla: I'm seeing GPU mem pressure on pool-embed-eu-1 and a rise in cold-KV-cache miss rate. A few requests retried, some hit fallback which increased latency. Looks like two heavy tenants spiked at ~08:12 UTC.

alice: customer impact? @dave can you surface any open support tickets or customer complaints?

dave: Support: 3 customer error reports in last 12m for embeddings failing with 502/timeout. IDs: CS-1199, CS-1201, CS-1203. All report delays in batch embed jobs. I've acknowledged and sent initial status: investigating.

erin: Product: priority customers listed in the PD alert are on the impacted list. Recommend short mitigation and a follow-up postmortem + customer note.

frank: I'm nearby, can take backup if needed.

alice: TL;DR: embeddings pool in EU hitting mem/scale limits -> requeues and latency. Immediate mitigations: 1) scale dedicated pool (if quota allows), 2) enable model-fallback to small-embed-128 for non-SLA customers, 3) apply transient rate-limit on heavy tenants. Who will run scale and who will flip fallback?

bob: I can attempt scale if we have quota. Trying a controlled horizontal scale now. Running:```bash
# scale pool
gcloud container clusters resize redwood-eu-embed --node-pool embed-nodes --num-nodes 18 --zone europe-west1-b
# or invoke autoscaler override
kubectl -n redwood-inference set env deployment/embed-autoscaler OVERRIDE_SCALE=18
```

carla: I'll prepare the fallback toggle. We have a quick flag in config-service: `embed.fallback.small_model=true` which forces non-critical routes to use `small-embed-128`. I'll stage it and flip after we confirm scale. Command:```bash
# flip fallback for non-SLA routes
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONFIG_TOKEN" \
  https://config.redwood/api/v1/flags/embed/fallback -d '{"value": "small-embed-128", "scope": "non-sla"}'
```

alice: Good. Bob please post success/failure of scale. Carla post when flag is live. I'll rate-limit heavy tenants via the routing rule for their API keys — quick patch:```json
{
  "route": "embed-tenant-heavy",
  "rate_limit": "50r/s"
}
```

bob: Scale command returned `QuotaExceeded` initially. I've opened a CC to infra-quota team and requested emergency quota bump. Meanwhile I bumped embed-autoscaler replica count to 6 (from 3) which gave modest relief. Observing CPU/GPU mem after bump.

ops-bot: auto-scaling event: embed-autoscaler replicas: 3 -> 6 (triggered by manual override) :white_check_mark:

carla: Fallback flag is staged in canary and rolling to 10% of traffic for non-SLA customers now. Canary logs look good (latency drop ~40% for those routes).

alice: Noted. After canary completes, flip to 100% for non-SLA. Meanwhile apply tenant rate-limits for the top 2 offending tenants (IDs t-981, t-771). Who has permission to change routing config? @bob?

bob: I can patch the route in the routing service. Doing quick patch now.```bash
# apply rate limit
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" \
  https://router.redwood/api/routes/embed-tenant-heavy -d '{"rate_limit": "50r/s"}'
```

bob: Patch applied. Monitoring metrics.

alice: Observability: p95 embeddings dropped from 2.5s -> 1.6s on non-SLA after canary. Overall p95 across EU improved to ~1.9s after replica bump + rate-limits. 5xx requeues decreased.

dave: I updated the three customers: short ETA ~20min, mitigation underway (scaling + fallback), offer to schedule follow-up once stable. Customers acknowledged.

erin: Good. Please capture the tenant patterns for postmortem — need to evaluate QoS/routing priorities and default fallback policies.

frank: infra-quota team responded: emergency GPU quota granted +4 vGPUs for cluster, ETA ~12 minutes for node provisioning.

alice: Outstanding actions and owners: 1) bob: confirm full-scale success and monitor (owner) 2) carla: flip fallback to 100% non-SLA after canary (owner) 3) dave: customer comms (owner) 4) erin: schedule postmortem & draft customer note (owner) 5) frank: followup with infra-quota until nodes online (owner). I'll update PD status and mark this incident as "mitigated" once p95 stable <2s for 30m.

bob: New nodes started joining cluster. Autoscaler target reached; embed pool at desired capacity. Seeing steady GPU utilization ~70%.

ops-bot: metric-alert cleared: EMBED_QUEUE_EU p95 latency back under threshold :white_check_mark:

alice: Marking PD status: acknowledged -> mitigated. Will keep thread open for 30m monitoring. Good job everyone.

carla: I'll spin up a follow-up evaluation job to replay recent workload against canary config to validate fallback behavior.

erin: I'll start drafting the customer update and a short RCA outline.

alice: Closing notes: primary root cause appears to be sudden tenant-driven spike combined with quota-limited autoscaler response. Action items include: stronger per-tenant throttles by default, fallback policies for embeddings, and playbook to request quota bump faster. I'll open tickets and assign owners post-incident. :spiral_note_pad:

dave: I'll keep CS tickets open until customers confirm recovery.

alice: Thanks. If any regressions, re-open PD page. Otherwise we meet in postmortem + retro tomorrow.
